flows.observation: Existing enrollment/heartbeat/workspace registry save host topology in fresh scopes. Legacy operation insert records payload/headers/body/version, conflict default hub-wins and fanout; retries/acknowledgments update operational queue/status, workspace paths/global IDs are mutable legacy fields.
flows.boundary: Retain legacy non-enrolled operation and records operationally with explicit cutover disposition. Do not treat mutable legacy GlobalWorkspaceId/path or default hub-wins replay as new immutable ProjectId or mandatory-review Dolt integration. Protected topology/queues/headers never become project payloads; no replay loop runs for enrolled projects.

flows.observation: Tools/buckets and agent adapters directly upsert/delete registry and agent/model/workspace rows in fresh contexts, copying payload/default timestamps.
flows.boundary: Existing host-local tools/agents remain operational and retained. Explicitly fence legacy replay for enrolled projects; merged history is not permission to install, launch, register or execute payloads. Source names and apply success do not prove correct protected destination or full child state.

flows.observation: Tool CRUD normalizes scope/tags and tombstones parents/tags; bucket add/remove/install/sync fetch manifests, create tool via registry, stamp provenance with later save, update installed definitions/tags and publish changes.
flows.boundary: Commands/templates, host/global tool scope, bucket provenance/sync status and tags stay operational. Keep delete/revival and scope behavior with actual child rows; never execute a command template or fetch/install merely from incoming project history. Preserve multi-save failures without claiming cross-store atomicity.

flows.observation: Database workspace update/delete normalizes local path, conditionally bootstraps, saves host registry or deletion metadata then writes filesystem projection and publishes change.
flows.boundary: Local registration, path, enablement/deletion and filesystem projection stay protected operational. Portable settings are only the approved separately sanitized projection. Local workspace deletion does not authorize deleting immutable project identity/history or portable content; preserve standalone semantics and original archives.

limitations: Source-anchor coverage is not semantic binding or complete dynamic caller closure
Original proposed classifications are retained without operator acceptance
All native routing and relational behavior remain unproven
No product, database, migration or deployment operation executes
